stories.summary: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." stories.headline: Engineering AI Discover
stories.summary: The challenges and decisions behind AI Discover’s intelligence layer By Varun Khaitan , Peng Ren , Gary Tang , Itay Teller , Atif Faheem , Nipun Kumar , Donnie DeBoer , Eduardo Lundgren , Matteo Rinaldi , Raghav Bakshi We recently introduced AI Discover , a new tab in our TV app where a small group of members can try new ways to find something to watch. For years, our recommendations have worked in the background, inferring what a member might enjoy from their viewing history.
stories.why_it_matters: AI Discover moves from that silent ranking toward steerable discovery. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Building AI Discover raised a question many teams will recognize: how do you deliver a better member experience with generative AI on TV without sacrificing speed, reliability or safety? Our answer is a new intelligence layer, the agent harness behind AI Discover.
Technical Implementation: For each request, it decides how to combine LLMs with our recommendation systems.
Deployment & Impact: It builds on years of work understanding what members enjoy, and on our recent work applying LLMs to recommendations and generative experiences.

stories.headline: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System
stories.summary: By Shreya S Ramanujam , Yongce Li , Afshine Amidi , Sina Ghiassian , Benjamin Klein. Introduction Picture this — you’re home after a long day at work and can’t wait to catch up on Bridgerton.
stories.why_it_matters: You log on to Netflix, search for “Bridgerton” and land on this screen: If this sounds familiar, you already know what a synopsis is — it’s a short glimpse into what a viewer can expect to see in a show. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: At Netflix’s scale, with thousands of titles, multiple episodes per season and multiple languages, fact-checking all of these by hand simply doesn’t scale.

Technical Implementation: Our current factuality checker feeds a reasoning model everything we know about a title (like metadata and text assets) and asks it to judge synopsis factuality according to a rigorous rubric.

Deployment & Impact: There are two main limitations of this approach that we want to optimize: High cost of long-context reasoning calls: Each decision requires expensive, long-context model calls to reasoning models, which doesn’t scale well when we want to check multiple titles, episodes, languages, and style variants.

stories.headline: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites

stories.headline: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down.
stories.why_it_matters: We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: All six models we test learn less in the chain: after eight generations it stands where the single agent stood after about four lives.
Technical Implementation: When each note is written from the full record of earlier lives instead of from the previous note, the same 300 characters recover 70% to 82% of the loss.
Deployment & Impact: The loss is robust across model sizes and is not alleviated by instructing the writer to record evidence, to revise the inherited note, or to keep a structured ledger.

stories.headline: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.18714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency.
stories.why_it_matters: Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2611.18714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases.
Technical Implementation: Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems.
Deployment & Impact: Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), for those refined capabilities.
